title: Regular finite root-stage system and its affine base change
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $k$ a field of characteristic $p$, $Y$ a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme, and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\to Y$ an affine etale chart [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in B$, $r\geq0$, cut out a reduced strict normal crossings boundary $V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ with its pairwise distinct reduced irreducible branches precisely $V(t_b)$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $I=\{n\in\mathbf Z_{>0}:(n,p)=1\}$, ordered by divisibility. Using multivariate polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], put
$$B_n=B[x_{1,n},\ldots,x_{r,n}]/(x_{b,n}^n-t_b)_b.$$
The transition $B_n\to B_m$ for $n\mid m$ sends $x_{b,n}$ to $x_{b,m}^{m/n}$. Fix $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and $a\notin J$, and put $u_J=\prod_{b\in J}t_b$, $C_n=B_n[1/u_J]$, $X_n=\operatorname{Spec}C_n$, $D_n=V(x_{a,n})\subset X_n$, and $W_n=X_n[1/t_a]$. Localization here is the universal ring in which the indicated element is invertible; affine schemes are as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then the following hold.

For $n\mid m$ and $e=m/n$, the natural presentation is
$$B_m\simeq B_n[y_1,\ldots,y_r]/(y_b^e-x_{b,n})_b,$$
and $B_m$ is free over $B_n$ with basis $\prod_b y_b^{d_b}$, $0\leq d_b<e$. The same basis gives freeness of $C_m$ over $C_n$; $B_n$ is free over $B$ with exponents $0\leq d_b<n$. Each $X_n$ and $D_n$ is regular Noetherian affine of finite type over $k$. Multiplication by $t_a$ and by $x_{a,n}$ on $C_n$ is injective. Thus $D_n$ is an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], with complement $W_n=X_n[1/x_{a,n}]$; its defining equation pulls back to $x_{a,m}^{m/n}$.

Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim_n C_n)$, the affine inverse limit, and $W=X[1/t_a]$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every affine pro-etale $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to V$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the projection $X'=X\times_VU\to X$ is affine pro-etale [def-pc-fibre-product]. If
$$T_R=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{n\in I}R[z_{1,n},\ldots,z_{r,n}]/(z_{b,n}^n-t_b)_b\right),$$
where $t_b$ denotes its image in $R$ and transitions are $z_{b,n}\mapsto z_{b,m}^{m/n}$, there is a canonical isomorphism of pairs over $U$
$$(X',W\times_X X')\simeq\bigl(T_R[1/u_J],T_R[1/(u_Jt_a)]\bigr).$$
It carries the principal open inclusion to the displayed principal open inclusion and the section $t_a$ to $t_a$. The statements allow the zero ring and empty coordinate divisors; for $r=0$ the finite-algebra assertions hold with empty monomial basis index (basis $1$), while no pair $(J,a)$ is allowed.

proof.text: The prime-to-p order is a unit over k and hence over B. Apply the finite-root-face regularity theorem to the empty and singleton faces. The empty face gives the full root ring by quotientBot; localization preserves regularity. For a singleton face, quotient localization identifies the localized coordinate quotient as a localization of the regular face. Use the top affine chart of the closed subscheme and Gamma-Spec to transfer regularity. Finite polynomial presentations, principal localization and the closed immersion provide finite type and quasi-compactness.

proof.text: Apply the proved SNC branch-equation nonzerodivisor theorem. The finite monomial basis makes the root algebra flat over B, and localization is flat, so multiplication by t_a stays injective. Since x_a^n=t_a, multiplication by x_a is injective. The canonical Gamma-Spec isomorphism carries this regular generator to the global-section generator of the coordinate ideal; IsInvertible.of_isAffine proves the Cartier assertion.

proof.text: For any compatible ring maps from the localized finite stages, restrict to the finite root quotients. Their coefficients agree through the order-one stage. Evaluate the full compatible-root polynomial quotient on the images of all labelled roots; the power and compatibility relations vanish. The denominator is a unit, so extend by Away.lift. Quotient and localization extensionality prove uniqueness. Apply the Gamma-Spec adjunction to the maps into the ring of global sections of any test scheme to obtain the scheme inverse-limit universal property.

proof.text: Prove the coefficient-change square for the full root algebra is a pushout directly: evaluate every new labelled root at the image of the old labelled root, and use agreement on coefficients for its power relation. Generator extensionality proves uniqueness. Principal localization is a pushout, and pasting gives the localized coefficient-change pushout. Taking spectra gives a pullback square and its canonical comparison isomorphism. Weak etaleness and affineness of the projection follow from scheme base-change instances.

proof.text: The pullback square fixes labelled roots and parameters by Gamma-Spec naturality. Inverting x and then y is the localization away from xy. Construct its open immersion using the canonical localization equivalence; its range is D(y). The pullback of the original principal open has this same range after the comparison isomorphism. The unique isomorphism of open immersions with equal ranges gives the pair comparison and its inclusion identity.
